_meta.description: FICTIONAL demo utility for testing UoF Business Plan Studio (Option A, playbook activities). Same utility and numbers as the Option B demo (Improvement scenario = the plan). All names and figures are invented.

states.midway: A1.1-A1.7 Approved, A2.1-A2.3 Submitted, A2.4 In progress, rest Not started; full data kept as examples for 'Fill with example'

utility.name: Valle Verde Water and Sanitation Company (DEMO)

preparation.implementation_strategy: TTL-led with a local consultant; plan starts 6 weeks after UoF completion.
preparation.resources: Local consultant 4 months; utility project team of 6

narratives.Commercial Management: Collection rose from 81% to 83% after the 100-day door-to-door campaign; metering grew to 66% but 34% of connections remain unmetered.
narratives.Technical Operations: NRW fell slowly from 45.1% to 43.0% through reactive leak repair only; continuity improved to 19 h/day.
narratives.Financial Management: Revenue grew 21% (2023-2025) with yearly tariff indexation; EBITDA margin improved to 18.2% and net income turned positive in 2025.
narratives.Human Talent: Staff fell from 795 to 780 by attrition; no structured training program.
narratives.Organization & Strategy: No strategic plan before the UoF; the UoF 100-day plan created a planning unit.

strengths.text: Committed management team after UoF 100-day plan

weaknesses.text: NRW of 43% with 34% of connections unmetered
No asset register or asset management plan

A1.3.management_discussion: Management agreed that losses and commercial efficiency explain most of the financial gap; human talent is the enabler for every other improvement.

A1.4.impact: Collection rose 1.5 points in 100 days after a door-to-door campaign in two districts; 1,200 illegal connections regularized.
A1.4.case_study: Door-to-door collection campaign in districts 3 and 7: 4,100 visits, 1,200 illegal connections regularized, USD 310,000 recovered.
A1.4.staff_engagement: High in commercial teams; field crews engaged once results were shared weekly.
lessons: Field data quality is the main bottleneck

A1.5.industrial_dynamics: Agro-processing park in the south adds 2 large industrial clients by 2027.
A1.5.infrastructure_development: Southern ring road opens new peri-urban settlements (about 8,000 households unserved).
A1.5.implications: Households grow faster than population (smaller households), so connections grow ~2.3%/yr; peri-urban growth to the south requires network expansion.

pillars.assessment: National water law sets cost-recovery principle; municipal politics delay decisions.
Weak coordination between municipality and region on peri-urban expansion.
Tariff indexation allowed up to inflation; access to national fund and IFI loans with sovereign guarantee.
opportunities: Tariff indexation; World Bank and national fund financing

pillars.assessment: Quality standards enforced; performance benchmarking published yearly.

weaknesses.text: Collection ratio of 83% and legacy billing system
High energy cost at pumping stations

opportunities.text: World Bank financing for NRW and sanitation
Tariff indexation to inflation allowed by regulator

threats.text: Drought periods reducing raw water availability

A1.7.management_discussion: Strategic workshop (2026-02-26): priorities are losses, collection and financing; drought risk handled through loss reduction rather than new sources.

A2.1.mission: Provide safe, reliable and affordable water and sanitation services to every household in Valle Verde, every day.
A2.1.vision: By 2035, to be the most efficient and trusted water utility in the region, with universal access and full cost recovery.

objectives.title: Reduce non-revenue water
objectives.specific: Reduce physical and apparent water losses across the network; Operations and Commercial departments.
objectives.measurable: NRW (%) from water balance: 43.0% in 2025 to 33.0% in 2030.
objectives.achievable: Funded by the World Bank loan; DMAs and meter replacement are proven in similar utilities.
objectives.relevant: Losses are the largest weakness in the SWOT and drive production cost and revenue.

objectives.title: Improve commercial efficiency
objectives.specific: Modernize billing and collection; Commercial department.
objectives.achievable: New CIS live by June 2027 and campaign proven in the 100-day plan (+1.5 points).
objectives.relevant: Supports financial sustainability and the mission of affordable service.

objectives.title: Strengthen financial sustainability
objectives.specific: Improve margins and keep debt service covered; Finance and Operations.
objectives.measurable: EBITDA margin 18.2% to at least 23%; DSCR above 1.5 every year; production cost per m3 8% below Baseline from 2028.
objectives.achievable: Driven by loss reduction, collection and efficient pumps.
objectives.relevant: Financial sustainability is a condition of the World Bank loan.

objectives.title: Expand access to services
objectives.specific: Extend water and sewer service to peri-urban areas; Planning department.
objectives.achievable: Network expansion and North WWTP rehabilitation financed by the loan.
objectives.relevant: Directly serves the mission of service for every household.

objectives.title: Develop human talent
objectives.specific: Train supervisors and technical staff in leadership and asset management; HR.
objectives.measurable: 100% of 64 supervisors and 120 technical staff trained.
objectives.achievable: USD 0.12 M per year program with a local university.
objectives.relevant: Human Talent is the lowest UoF maturity score (39/100).

charters.mission: Cut physical losses by sectorizing the network into 24 district metered areas with pressure control.
charters.scope: Design and install 24 DMAs, 40 pressure-reducing valves, flow meters and SCADA links.

charters.mission: Meter every connection accurately to bill real consumption.
charters.scope: Procure and install 60,000 class C meters; update customer database.

charters.mission: Replace the 2004 billing system and raise collection.
charters.scope: CIS implementation, data migration, mobile collection, campaign.

charters.mission: Cut energy use in pumping with high-efficiency pumps and variable speed drives.
goals: Production cost per m3 8% below Baseline from 2028
charters.scope: Replace 9 pumps at 3 stations; install VFDs; energy monitoring.

charters.mission: Restore treatment capacity to enable 3,000 new sewer connections.
Connect 8,000 households in unserved southern neighborhoods.
Build leadership and asset management skills in supervisors and technical staff.
charters.scope: Training curriculum with a local university; 184 participants.

A3.2.note: Proforma assumptions already include the effects of the initiatives (NRW, collection, connections, production cost).

A3.3.conclusions: Tariffs are the critical variable: a 10% tariff shortfall lowers 2030 EBITDA by about USD 1.3 M and DSCR stays at 1.28 or more; a 20% shock pushes DSCR below 1.0 in 2026 (0.92), the year with the highest debt service relative to cash. The utility will request yearly indexation and protect collection gains.

A3.4.executive_summary: Valle Verde (fictional) serves about 487,000 people with water (89% coverage) and 370,000 with sewerage. NRW of 43% and collection of 83% limit its finances. The plan invests USD 18.7 M in seven actions (2026-2030), financed with a USD 14 M World Bank loan and own funds. By 2030 it targets NRW 33%, collection 93%, EBITDA margin about 24% and DSCR above 1.5, while lowering the tariff needed for cost recovery compared with the Baseline.
A3.4.water_balance_discussion: Production can stay nearly flat to 2030 despite 19% more connections because losses fall 10 points.
A3.4.asset_management_plan: Asset register to be built in 2027 (deferred priority); investment plan focuses on DMAs, meters, pumps, WWTP and expansion.

A4.1.dashboard_rules: Commercial and Operations upload quarter data by the 10th working day; Planning unit validates by the 15th.

A4.2.transition: Consultant handed over on 2026-06-30; planning unit owns the tracking.

A4.3.summary: Plan shared with staff, board, regulator and the public between July and August 2026.
